about.title: Santa Ana Product Liability Claims
about.longDescription: A product does not have to be exotic to hurt someone. In Santa Ana, these claims tend to begin with everyday things: a space heater in a Bristol Street apartment, a power tool bought off the shelf, a child's car seat, a medication whose label left out a serious risk, or an airbag that never deployed during one of the 1,708 injury collisions recorded across the city in 2025. When a defect in how the item was designed, built, or labeled causes harm, California law lets the injured person pursue the manufacturer, the distributor, and the retailer, often without proving anyone was careless. We listen to what happened and handle your case directly. Our team works on contingency, so there is no fee unless there is a recovery. Your part is simple: hold onto the product, the packaging, and any receipts, and get your injuries looked at.

whyChoose.title: Why Santa Ana Residents Choose Us

items.title: Strict liability changes the question
items.desc: In California you generally do not have to show the maker was negligent, only that the product had a design, manufacturing, or warning defect and that the defect caused your injury. Our team knows how to frame the case around that standard.

items.title: Every link in the chain matters
items.desc: Manufacturers, distributors, and retailers can all be responsible for a defective product under California law. We can trace who touched the item on its way to a Santa Ana store or doorstep.

items.title: Evidence starts with the product itself
items.desc: Throwing the item away, letting a repair shop keep it, or accepting a replacement can weaken a claim. We will point you toward preservation right away and arrange proper inspection.

items.question: I bought the product at a store in Santa Ana, but it was made overseas. Who can I hold responsible?
items.answer: You are not limited to the factory. Under California product liability law, the retailer that sold it and the distributor that brought it into Orange County can share liability along with the manufacturer. That is one reason your receipt and packaging are worth keeping. We can sort out which parties belong in the claim.

items.question: Do I have to prove the company did something wrong?
items.answer: Usually not. California product liability often runs on strict liability, meaning you generally need to show the product was defective in its design, manufacturing, or warnings and that the defect caused your injury. Whether the company was careless is a separate question and is often not required. Our team can explain which theory fits your situation.

items.question: What if a defective car part contributed to my crash on I-5 or 1st Street?
items.answer: A collision can involve both a driver's conduct and a product failure, such as brakes, tires, or an airbag that did not deploy. Those are separate claims that may run side by side. The vehicle and the failed component need to be preserved before they are repaired or scrapped, so contact us early. There is no cost for the case review, and we work on contingency.
